tagline: Scheduling chaos and a quiet Instagram
raw_input: I run a small coffee shop near the UMD campus. 6 employees, mostly students, and their class schedules change every semester so I spend like 4 hours a week just redoing the schedule and texting people to cover shifts. Our Instagram has been dead for months because I don't have time to post. Afternoons between 2 and 5 are super slow on weekdays and I'd love to get students in then. We use Square for the register. I can maybe spend $150 a month on software. I'm OK with apps on my phone but I'm not a computer guy.

tagline: Missed calls while on the job
raw_input: We're a 4-tech HVAC company. Biggest problem: when my guys are on a job and I'm on a roof, nobody answers the phone. I think we miss 15-20 calls a week in summer and a new AC install is worth $6-8k, a repair maybe $350. Quotes take me forever, I write them at night on paper and type them up, maybe 6 hours a week. Invoices are paper too and customers pay slow. We use QuickBooks for the books and Google Calendar for scheduling. Budget is around $300 a month if it pays for itself. I'm decent with tech.

tagline: Quoting and routing a seasonal crew
raw_input: Landscaping company, me plus a seasonal crew of 8 from March to November. In spring we get flooded with quote requests and I drive out to every property to measure, then write the estimate by hand — I lose jobs because I'm too slow to respond, probably 5-6 jobs a month at around $1,200 each. Routing the crew each morning is a mess, they waste time driving back and forth. We get paid by check mostly. I don't use any software besides a spreadsheet and texting. I'd spend $200 a month. Keep it simple, I'm not great with computers.
